about: What scripts/sign.mjs signs in the app's payload (Contents/Resources), inside-out, with the hardened runtime: every Mach-O file of the payload must be named here (a file entry, or the main executable of a bundle entry) or the bundle fails — a new native dependency is added on purpose. `entitlements`: a plist of entitlements/ (release); `dryDLV`: the ad hoc (dry) signature adds disable-library-validation, which an executable loading code of another signature needs when no team identifies both (ad hoc has none). Paths are relative to Resources; * stands for one path segment or part of one. The entitlements are the least an ad hoc probe proved (DESIGN §4p: Node.js JITs with allow-jit); what no offline probe can prove stays: Node.js keeps disable-library-validation in release (the person's own native addons, in hooks or sandbox scripts, carry another signature than the app's). The app carries no browser and no compositor: they are downloaded Tools (apps/desktop/bundle/tools.json), never signed by the app.
